source.title: Examining Language Model Performance with Reconstructed Activations using Sparse Autoencoders

page_placements.theme: Error varies across tokens, positions, contexts and input conditions

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effects of replacing model activations with SAE reconstructions on model performance, using benchmark outcomes rather than directly measuring the dark-matter properties in the claim.
record.gate_note: The post reports intervention and benchmark outcomes relevant to whether SAE reconstruction errors affect model behavior. It does not compare reconstruction errors with random errors of the same size, and it does not measure linear predictability or compare SAE sizes. Individual plot values are not given in the text.
record.test_reason: The post patches SAE reconstructions into gpt2-small and reports downstream loss and benchmark accuracy. It has no random-error comparison of matched norm (V3's defining contrast), no linear prediction of the error (V1, V4), no comparison across SAE sizes since all SAEs share one width (V2), no circuit or steering analysis with and without the error term (V5), and no alternative training method (V6). Its results show SAE reconstructions degrade performance, strongly so beyond the training context. That is a related construct, reconstruction quality and its dependence on context length, layer and task, not a test of any version. It also predates the original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs perform poorly beyond their training context, and that training on longer contexts is low-hanging fruit. Within the training context, performance falls with layer, which they suggest may reflect fixed width against more features in later layers. Beyond it, early layers (about 2–4) are worst. CE on random tokens does not map one-to-one onto task performance, so task benchmarks are needed. The 'quasi-random' remark refers to the absence of a prompt-level effect, not to a comparison with random errors.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE residual-stream reconstructions as interventions in gpt2-small, but evaluates downstream cross-entropy and benchmark behavior rather than measuring dark-matter structure or comparing errors across SAE sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with context length and layer; performance differs between Lambada and the longer-context Children’s Book Test.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE reconstruction quality and downstream ΔCE degrade sharply beyond the SAE training context (128 tokens), worst in early layers. Within that context, degradation grows with layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error depends strongly on context position relative to the SAE training context, and on layer.

fits_no_version.finding: CE loss on random tokens does not map onto task accuracy. Lambada and CBT show different layer trends, and patching harm on Lambada shows no consistent prompt-level pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The downstream impact of SAE reconstruction error is task-dependent and is not captured by CE on random tokens.

record.problems: No random-error comparison of matched size; uncertainty estimates are not reported in the text; several outcomes are available only in plots, without text-extracted values. The post notes that an earlier version of the second figure had a bug and was fixed.
record.rows_left_out: Per-layer plotted values for Open WebText, Lambada, and CBT were not separately transcribed because the text supplies no exact values for them and the plotted values are not text-extracted. The records retain the narrated aggregate or layer-group results.

untested.parts: All: no linear regression of the SAE error on the input activation.
All: a single SAE width per layer, so no cross-size error-norm prediction or context overlap.
Comparison of SAE-patching harm against random errors of equal norm.
All: no split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts, and no learnability test.
All: no circuit or steering analysis with and without the error term (IOI is listed only as future work).
All: no alternative architectures or objectives. A commenter only suggests end-to-end training.

missing.what: Error propagation: upstream SAE patching raises downstream SAE reconstruction MSE and ℓ0, especially for the layer 9 SAE. Reported as fractional changes in a heatmap.
Per-feature mean Δlnp and score histograms: most features are active when patching hurts, with a small helpful tail.
missing.locator: Lambada section, feature histograms; CBT appendix

missing.what: Local SAE metrics (ℓ0, MSE, ℓ1) versus context position and layer on Open WebText, plus MSE versus residual ℓ2 norm (no strong norm dependence).
missing.locator: How does context length affect SAE performance...; first and third figures

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V3, but V3's defining claim is harm beyond norm-matched random errors, which this post never tests. Showing that reconstruction harms loss is necessary but not sufficient, so the rows are relinked to none. The post (Feb 2024) predates the original source (Oct 2024). The ΔCE metric is noted in the comments to differ subtly from KL divergence. A figure bug was fixed after publication.

versions.untested_parts: No linear prediction of the SAE error vector from input activations is measured.
No cross-size comparison of per-token error norms or token/context overlap is made.
The post measures harms from SAE reconstruction interventions but does not compare them with random errors of the same size.
The post does not separate linear and nonlinear error components or test their learnability.
No circuits or steering analyses are tested with and without the error term.
No alternative SAE architecture, training objective, or end-to-end training method is compared.

relation.reason: It discusses missing SAE information and possible training explanations, but its experiments establish related reconstruction failures rather than a specified dark-matter claim.

tranche.reason: The study measures reconstruction and downstream benchmark degradation without testing any specified claim version. It lacks matched-norm random-error controls, error-prediction or scaling tests, circuit or steering analyses, and training-method comparisons.

source_check.notes: Exact plotted losses are unavailable in the text; CBT accuracy approximations are explicitly stated. Longer-context training is proposed, not experimentally shown to fix the errors.
